items.title: What to Know About the Banking Service Outages Impacting Thousands of Customers
items.standfirst: Thousands of customers at multiple major U.S. banks are reporting problems afterJPMorgan Chase said it was experiencing a technical issue.
items.content: Chase bank branch sign on building in San Francisco, California, on March 25, 2026. —Smith Collection—Gado/Getty ImagesThousands of customers at multiple major U.S. banks are reporting difficulties accessing banking services on Monday after JPMorgan Chase announced a technical issue impacting its systems. “JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems – there is no evidence this is cyber-related,” the company, which has over 86 million customers across the U.S., wrote on X. “It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.”“We’re working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today,” it added.JPMorgan Chase did not immediately respond to TIME’s request for additional information regarding the issue.Here’s what we know.Which banks and services are being impacted?Beyond Chase, customers at several other banks—including Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Capital One, and Truist—have reported problems on Monday, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.com. Issues were also reported with digital money transfer service Zelle.JPMorgan Chase noted that other banks where it was “party to a transaction” may also be impacted by the technical issue it is experiencing. But it added that “this is not a systemic issue.” The company also said that its customers retained access to their accounts and money. Zelle said in a statement to news outlets that its service is "operating as it should," but that "an issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers." “Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds,” a spokesperson for the company said. “Consumers do not have a separate Zelle account, and Zelle does not hold consumer funds. An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers. Please contact them directly.”Zelle is owned and operated by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which is itself jointly owned by financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank, and Capital One.A U.S. Bank spokesperson said to multiple outlets that “U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted,” but that “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”How widespread are the outages?Many Chase customers reportedly received a message on Monday that said “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”By around 2 p.m. Eastern time, more than 4,700 customers at the bank had reported experiencing problems, according to Downdetector.com.Reports of issues at other banks spiked around the same time, with just over 2,000 outage reports at Bank of America and 1,060 at U.S. Bank, per the site. Hundreds of customers at Wells Fargo, Capitol One, Truist, and Zelle also reported issues Monday afternoon.

items.title: United Airlines Experiences Temporary System Outage in the Wake of Nationwide Ground Stop
items.standfirst: The airline confirmed that the issue that delayed departing flights on Monday has since been resolved.
items.content: A United Airlines plane lands near the control tower at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on Nov. 16, 2026. —Joe Raedle—Getty ImagesUnited Airlines has resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights on Monday afternoon, three days after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop that has continued to impact flights around the country.United Airlines confirmed in a statement to TIME on Monday evening that there was a “technology issue that delayed flight departures” that had since been resolved. The airline added that “some flights were delayed” but that the issue didn’t affect flights in the air or its regional network. The airline said that “there is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue” but didn’t provide additional details about the technology issue it had experienced.About an hour before TIME received the statement, United Airlines had said in social media posts to customers that it was “aware of the widespread system outage.”The outage follows the nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA that lasted for hours on Friday because of a telecommunications outage. The nation’s air travel system is still recovering from the nationwide stoppage—as of Monday evening, more than 5,000 flights within, into, or out of the U.S. had been delayed and 349 had been canceled, according to FlightAware.The flight-tracking website showed that almost 600 United flights experienced delays on Monday as of the early evening.The ongoing delays and cancellations come ahead of an anticipated Thanksgiving travel rush next week, when AAA has projected that nearly 6 million people will travel by air in the U.S.
